title: Design a Text Editor with Undo
summary: Build an editor whose every edit is a reversible command, where consecutive keystrokes coalesce into one undo step, replace-all undoes as a single action, and a new edit after an undo correctly discards the redo stack.
concepts: Command versus Memento for undo, and the memory trade between them
Why a new edit must clear the redo stack
Coalescing keystrokes so undo matches what a user considers one action
Composite commands undoing in reverse order
Capturing inverse data at execute time, not construction time
Bounding the undo stack so a long session is not a leak
extensions: Add a piece table or rope so large files do not copy the whole string
Support multiple cursors editing at once
Add collaborative editing with operational transforms or CRDTs
Add syntax highlighting as a decorator over the document
Persist the undo history across sessions
Add a non-linear undo tree rather than a single stack
